milestones.name: On the mixed-mesh field, Occlusion draws only what Direct shows, pixel for pixel

items.statement: A scene that selects meshes runs Occlusion: preparation no longer refuses it, and every frame is byte-equal to bucket-ordered Direct while the bucket layout churns behind cover (class flips, deactivation, compaction).
items.ask: Read the tests this check runs. Do they compare every frame with bucket-ordered Direct, assert that Occlusion is the resolved mode and hides at least one slot, and fail under each mutant the design names: a two-sided prepass on a back-culled open mesh, and the final draw reading the prepass list?

items.statement: Along the mixed-mesh field flythrough, Occlusion is byte-equal to bucket-ordered Direct at every tick through the first cut, never draws more than Frustum, and hides at least half of Frustum's list on some counted tick.

A mesh whose face lies on its own bounds, flush with a prepass occluder at a rounded far pose, keeps every tied pixel under the derived tolerance and the widened footprint. A cull with zero depth tolerance loses pixels there. The footprint widening has its own witness, or a record that the reference's search found none.
items.ask: Which witness exercises the depth slack and which the footprint widening? Does the evidence hold the zero-depth-tolerance mutant failing on the mesh tie witness (a cube witness does not answer this), and for the widening either a no-widening mutant failing on its witness or the poses searched without finding one?

items.statement: After a surface resize and after device replacement, with slots hidden behind cover on the mixed-mesh field, Occlusion still equals bucket-ordered Direct and still hides slots.
items.ask: Does a test in this target resize the surface and replace the device while slots are hidden, and compare the next frames with the oracle?

items.statement: APPLE-TILE's M0 exact matrix passes on a release build of the claimed commit: this milestone moved no retained Mac image. Chrome's baseline is not checked here; the design says when it is.
items.check: cargo build --locked --offline --release -p v1-game --features draw-probe,thrum-render/creation-counters && cargo build --locked --offline --release -p thrum-cook && rm -rf tmp/exact-m0 && mkdir -p tmp/exact-m0 && target/release/thrum-cook cook examples/v1-game/assets/showcase tmp/exact-m0/valley && python3 scripts/apple_tile_m1.py --store tmp/exact-m0/valley --output tmp/exact-m0/m1 && python3 scripts/apple_tile_m2.py --store tmp/exact-m0/valley --output tmp/exact-m0/m2

milestones.quality_bar: Culling as in a shipped GPU-driven renderer, where nothing visible ever disappears or pops; held here to byte equality with drawing everything, on meshes of a few hundred to a few thousand triangles.

milestones.name: The game picks its culling mode from the device and the measurements, and says which mode ran

items.statement: A requested culled mode resolves to Direct when the capability record lacks adapter-read indirect execution or its facts are unknown. The resolved mode and the reason are reported, and no pass queries the device.
items.ask: Trace the mode from the request to the prepared pipelines. Is the capability record its only input, and do the existing equality tests assert the resolved mode, so a fallback cannot pass as culling?

items.statement: On the iPhone simulator the game runs with a culled mode requested, reports Direct with the capability reason, and draws the complete scene. Function only.
In Chrome, Frustum and Occlusion on the mixed-mesh field are each byte-equal to Chrome's bucket-ordered Direct at the 16 oracle views, and Occlusion draws fewer than Frustum at a view behind cover.

The mixed-mesh field's default mode follows the design's rule: paired whole-GPU rows for Direct, Frustum and Occlusion at 1920x1080, behind cover and in the open, from two separate runs, are recorded with their load, and the default is Occlusion only if it wins in both.
items.ask: Do the two retained run logs support the default the code sets, by the design's rule? Does the bench assert that Occlusion's prepass is non-empty and that it hides slots, so a row cannot repeat the fault that withdrew the rows of 8 November?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this milestone moved no retained image.

milestones.quality_bar: A renderer that picks its path from device facts and says which one ran, as Unreal's mobile path and Unity's fallback do: a device that cannot run a culled mode still draws the whole scene, and a default is never set on a guess.

milestones.name: The valley's 10,000 entities are culled by default and match the unculled image pixel for pixel, on Mac and in Chrome

items.statement: With the valley's default culling mode, every submitted frame of the moving route equals the same route drawn Direct, on both native recipes.
In Chrome, with the valley's default culling mode, every checkpoint of the moving route equals the same route drawn Direct.
The valley's default mode is set by the design's rule from paired rows on the moving route, recorded with their load and the reason.
items.ask: Do the retained rows support the valley's default mode by the design's rule, and does the game report that mode on the Mac and in Chrome?

items.statement: With meshes selected for the valley's entities, Frustum and Occlusion on the bucket route, with Sun-caster culling, equal bucket-ordered Direct along the moving route on the Mac.
In Chrome, with meshes selected for the valley's entities, Frustum and Occlusion equal bucket-ordered Direct at the moving route's checkpoints.
With temporal sampling selected, Frustum and Occlusion stay byte-equal to Direct over a full jitter cycle.

On the Mac, with the valley's default culling mode, no frame the game submits while it runs in real time shows a culling artifact: nothing pops in or out, flickers or is missing at a frame edge during a fast yaw, or at an occluder's silhouette when the camera steps out of cover. The item is about what each submitted frame holds. How fast or how evenly the frames arrive is not part of it.
items.inspect: Capture the valley with T2 engine capture, with the game reporting its default mode: `fixed` stills at the moving route's checkpoints and a `realtime` pan with fast yaw. Add the mixed-mesh field's retained per-tick frames through cover and back out, which are fixed-time readback. Judge whole frames and native-size crops at the frame edges, the ridge line and around walls and props, as consecutive submitted frames at 1x. Use a realtime capture that holds every submitted frame, because an omitted frame cannot show what it held. Read that capture as a sequence of images only. It is taken under load with the capture observer on, so its submission intervals, gaps and frame rate count neither for nor against this item, and the target's full-refresh edge condition is not run for it. The design's 'Frame cadence' section says who judges smoothness.

items.statement: In Chrome, with the valley's default culling mode, no frame the page submits while it runs in real time shows a culling artifact: nothing pops in or out, flickers or is missing at a frame edge or at an occluder's silhouette on the valley route. The item is about what each submitted frame holds. How fast or how evenly the frames arrive is not part of it.
items.inspect: Capture the valley in Chrome with T2 engine capture, with the page reporting its default mode: `fixed` at the moving route's checkpoints and a `realtime` pan. Judge whole frames and native-size crops at the frame edges and the ridge line, as consecutive submitted frames at 1x. Use a realtime capture that holds every submitted frame, because an omitted frame cannot show what it held. Read that capture as a sequence of images only. Its recorder runs headless on a 60 Hz timer, under load, so its submission intervals, gaps and frame rate count neither for nor against this item, and the target's full-refresh edge condition is not run for it. The design's 'Frame cadence' section says who judges smoothness.

items.statement: Gate G3c holds as the brief words it, and the maturity ledger says what was and was not proved.
items.ask: Does each clause of gate G3c in the brief hold on main, with evidence linked from docs/evidence/CULLING/: compute frustum and Hi-Z culling; GPU-written indirect instance counts; one indexed indirect draw per mesh and pipeline bucket; stable mesh offsets; a material table that compute can read; visibility and image equivalence; full- and partial-visibility costs recorded as tripwires? Is the ledger's G3c row current, with implementation, correctness, visuals and device results kept apart?

items.statement: The coverage output, every exact reference it moved and their registry pins reached main in one merge. Each moved reference is regenerated by `APPLE-TILE`'s own scripts from a build that holds the output. In `.config/exact-baselines.json` that merge changed the `pin` and the `refresh` of each baseline whose reference moved, each refresh naming `ruling-on-culling-m3`, `CULLING` and `M3`, and nothing else; the comparisons, their sampling and every script are as they were. The references replaced were what main drew, and main draws the new ones at the claimed commit. `APPLE-TILE`'s log and this module's each record the cause and every moved reference's old and new SHA-256.
items.ask: Read the diff that merge made to `.config/exact-baselines.json` yourself with `git diff`: does it change only the `pin` and the `refresh` of the baselines whose references moved, with each refresh naming `ruling-on-culling-m3`, `CULLING` and `M3`? Did the coverage output, the moved references and those pins reach main in that one merge, with the comparison scripts and their sampling as they were, and has no other merge of this module changed a registered reference? Does the evidence hold a passing verifier record, the builder's or the main-branch check's, at the commit of main the references were regenerated on top of? Do both logs list each moved reference's old and new SHA-256 and say which of the five sets moved? The order in which the builder made its proofs before the merge is not part of this item.

items.statement: Under GPU load the merged build draws one image on the pipelines M3.1 and M3.4 compare. In one interleaved campaign on a build of main, as the design's 'Proof that it is one image' describes it, a control that differs only by leaving out the coverage output differs between hosts in at least five routes, and the build with the output differs in none over at least as many routes, with every combination of the two recipes, the two sources and the two entity routes run by both. The commit the campaign's binaries were built from is on main and holds the landing and every change this milestone merged to what the game is built from.
items.ask: Does the retained campaign record meet the design's rule under 'Proof that it is one image': complete routes taken in turn with the control, four hosts, two counted render workers, the full exact comparison at every tick, every combination of the two recipes, the two sources and the two entity routes (cubes and selected meshes) run by both builds, the control differing in at least five routes and the build with the output in none over at least as many? Does the control's source differ from the campaigned commit's only by the coverage output? Check with git yourself: is the commit the record names an ancestor of main's tip, does it contain the merge that landed the coverage output, and does `git log` from it to the claimed commit, over `crates/`, `examples/v1-game/`, `.cargo/`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `rust-toolchain.toml`, show no commit of this milestone's? A campaign made on the branch before the merge does not answer this item. Commits other modules merged after the campaigned commit are not part of it.

items.statement: Only shared triangle edges moved the references. Where a refreshed Mac reference differs from the one it replaces, the pixel lies along an edge between triangles of opaque geometry. The sky, the stars and the letterbox bars hold their old bytes, and no difference fills a triangle's interior. In Chrome, where only digests are retained, the same is shown between captures of the starting commit and captures whose digests are the refreshed ones, for each set that moved.
items.inspect: From the retained Mac references at the starting commit and at the claimed commit, make an image of where the bytes differ, amplified, for the route's five checkpoints and the Sun and night stills, in SDR and in scene-linear. Judge each beside its frame, whole and in native-size crops: thin lines that follow the terrain's and the props' triangle edges, none in the sky, among the stars or in the bars, and no filled patch. Read the builder's Chrome difference images the same way for each Chrome set that moved, and the count of differing pixels and the largest difference for each reference.

items.statement: The coverage output's cost on the valley's moving route is recorded: paired, interleaved rows of the claimed shader and the control without the output, per pass and for the whole frame, p50 and p95, from two runs with their load and workload identities, on both native recipes. Where the rows cross a tripwire in the design's Performance section, the evidence holds an investigation of the cause and its disposition. No figure is a pass mark.
items.ask: Do the retained rows pair the claimed shader with a control that differs only by the coverage output, on the moving route on both native recipes, from two runs with the load and workload identities recorded, and does the maturity ledger carry them as a recorded cost, not a budget? If the whole frame's paired p50 crossed the tripwire in the design's Performance section, does the evidence say which passes carry the cost and why, and record one of the design's two dispositions? A crossed tripwire with that record passes this item.

milestones.quality_bar: Culling as in a shipped open-world game such as Horizon Forbidden West: the player never sees it work. Flying the valley and the field, nothing pops, flickers or goes missing at a screen edge or at an occluder's silhouette, in any frame the game submits. The project bar's 'smooth at the display's full refresh' is not judged in this milestone: `SHOWCASE` judges it on the culled exit scene, as the design's 'Frame cadence' section says.
